q: How does a ship recycling plot in Alang work out its emissions?
title: Alang ship recycling plot: emissions
short: Most direct emissions come from LPG burnt in cutting torches and diesel in winches, cranes and vehicles. Add electricity from the bill. Divide by tonnes of steel recovered, or by light displacement tonnes of the ship. Oxygen used with the torches is bought in, so its emissions sit in Scope 3.
audience: Ship recycling plots at Alang and Sosiya and their steel buyers

ul: LPG cylinders or bulk LPG for cutting.
Diesel for winches, cranes and trucks.

p: Re-rollers and steel buyers increasingly want a figure for the plate they buy. Keep tonnes recovered per ship.

example.title: Worked example
lines: LPG: 18 t for one ship x 2.98 kg = 53.6 t CO2
Diesel: 25,000 L x 2.68 kg = 67.0 t CO2
Steel recovered: 9,000 t, so about 13 kg CO2 per tonne

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
